page: UpCloud STARTER-1xCPU-4GB is a starter-tier virtual server configured on the KVM hypervisor. It features a single shared vCPU mapped to one physical core and one thread, utilizing an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory and includes 30 GB of local SSD storage, alongside one complimentary public IPv4 address. No dedicated GPU hardware is present on this instance.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-threaded and multi-threaded performance. The server achieves top-tier results in single-core metrics, including stress-ng single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and Geekbench single-core execution. However, due to its single shared vCPU configuration, multi-core performance is weak, as demonstrated by low multi-core Geekbench and stress-ng scores. Memory read bandwidth and database operations also rank in the lower percentiles, while memory write bandwidth for large blocks remains average.

This server represents a budget-friendly resource profile, trading off multi-core processing power and high memory bandwidth for cost-effective single-core performance. It is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded workloads such as basic text processing, simple utility scripting, low-traffic web serving, or small-scale development and testing environments. It is not recommended for multi-threaded compilation, database-heavy operations, or resource-intensive applications.
